title: Applied Practice: Access Gate Assessment
description: Multiple-choice assessment for Applied Practice: Access Gate.

questions.question: Why should serious rejection rules often come first in an access gate?

options.text: They prevent invalid users from reaching later checks
They force every branch to run
They remove the need for else

questions.explanation: Blocking rules such as login or restriction status should be handled before success logic.

questions.question: What is a benefit of giving each rejection branch a clear message?

options.text: The user understands why access was denied

questions.explanation: Specific messages improve usability and make the decision easier to debug.

questions.question: What does the final else usually represent in an access gate?

options.text: The success path after all rejection checks failed
The first error in the program

questions.explanation: After all blocking conditions are handled, else can safely grant access.

questions.question: Which test strategy is best for an access gate?

options.text: Test each branch with separate input values

questions.explanation: Each branch should be tested so you know every response can occur correctly.
